title: Granny-style hexagon
subtitle: The hexagonal version of the classic granny motif — cluster groups at six corners, side clusters from round 3
excerpt: The granny-style hexagon works cluster groups of three trebles at all six corners and adds side clusters from round 3 onward, matching the granny square's visual texture. Four rounds give a 12 cm point-to-point motif that sits comfortably alongside granny squares in mixed blankets.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Crochet, Volumes 1-3 (1885-1890) — the hexagonal motif constructions (Internet Archive). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), crochet motif chapter.
heroPrompt: A granny-style crochet hexagon in warm cream DK cotton on a linen background, photographed flat from above in soft natural light — the 12 cm motif shows six corner cluster pairs and one side cluster between each corner pair on the outer round.

crochet.gaugeText: Each finished four-round granny-style hexagon measures 12 cm point-to-point in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook, after a light steam-block.

glossaryTerms.definition: Three trebles worked into the same chain-space, joined at the top. The basic building block of granny-style motifs.
The gap created by skipping a chain or chains. Corner chain-2 spaces hold the corner cluster pairs; side chain-1 spaces separate cluster pairs along the sides.

content.text: The granny-style hexagon applies the granny square's
cluster
construction to a six-sided motif: the same (3tr, ch 2, 3tr) corner groups at all six
chain-space

corners, and side cluster groups between the corners from round 3 onward. Four rounds give a 12 cm point-to-point motif with two side clusters per edge — visually consistent with a four-round granny square and able to join alongside squares in the same blanket with only minor gap-filling at the corners.

The main thing to hold in your head is that the repeat is six instead of four. Every other aspect of the method is the same as a standard granny square. Placing a stitch marker in the first corner ch-2 space at the start of each round makes it easier to count the six repeats correctly.

attrs.title: Materials for one motif
attrs.body: About 7 g of DK-weight cotton in one to four colours. A 4 mm crochet hook (UK 8, US G/6). Tapestry needle. Scissors. A blocking mat and pins — hexagons need their six points pinned to stay symmetrical.

content.text: Gauge
Each finished four-round granny-style hexagon measures 12 cm point-to-point in DK-weight cotton with a 4 mm hook, after a light steam-block. Make a test motif before starting a grid project.
Stitches used
chain (ch) — UK and US shared.
slip stitch (sl st) — UK and US shared.
treble (tr) — UK; called double crochet (dc) in US patterns.
magic ring (MR) — adjustable starting loop; no centre hole.
Pattern
Worked in the round, right side facing throughout. Ch 3 at the start of each round counts as the first treble of the first cluster. Do not turn.
Round 1

Form a magic ring. Ch 3 (counts as first tr). Work 2 tr into the ring. *Ch 2, 3 tr into the ring*; repeat from * to * four more times. Ch 2, sl st to top of beg ch-3 to join. Pull tail to close ring. (18 tr, 6 ch-2 corner spaces.)
Round 2

Sl st across next 2 tr and into first ch-2 corner sp. Ch 3. Into same sp work 2 tr, ch 2, 3 tr. *Ch 1, into next ch-2 corner sp work (3 tr, ch 2, 3 tr)*; repeat from * to * four more times. Ch 1, sl st to top of beg ch-3 to join. (36 tr, 6 ch-2 corner spaces, 6 ch-1 side spaces.)
Round 3

Sl st into first ch-2 corner sp. Ch 3. Into same sp work 2 tr, ch 2, 3 tr. Ch 1. *Into next ch-1 side sp work 3 tr. Ch 1. Into next ch-2 corner sp work (3 tr, ch 2, 3 tr). Ch 1.* Repeat from * to * four more times. Into next ch-1 side sp work 3 tr. Ch 1. Sl st to top of beg ch-3 to join. (54 tr, 6 ch-2 corner spaces, 12 ch-1 side spaces.)
Round 4

Sl st into first ch-2 corner sp. Ch 3. Into same sp work 2 tr, ch 2, 3 tr. Ch 1. *[Into next ch-1 side sp work 3 tr. Ch 1.] twice. Into next ch-2 corner sp work (3 tr, ch 2, 3 tr). Ch 1.* Repeat from * to * four more times. [Into next ch-1 side sp work 3 tr. Ch 1.] twice. Sl st to top of beg ch-3 to join. (72 tr, 6 ch-2 corner spaces, 18 ch-1 side spaces.)
Chart
The chart reads outward from the magic ring. Six corner chain-2 spaces are marked throughout; side cluster groups sit between them from round 3.

definition.title: Granny-style hexagon
definition.caption: Four rounds from the magic ring. Six corner ch-2 spaces throughout. Round 4 has two side clusters per edge and 72 trebles total.

content.text: Finishing

Fasten off, leaving a 15 cm tail. Weave through 3 to 4 stitches on the wrong side, reverse direction through 2 to 3 stitches, and trim. Weave in the magic ring tail. Steam-block on a foam mat with all six points pinned symmetrically.
Joining

The granny-style hexagon joins along its six sides in the same way as the basic hexagon: whip-stitch or flat sl-st seam through the back loops, matching side clusters along each edge. When mixing with granny squares, use a half-hexagon or small triangle motif to fill the gaps at the corners where hexagons and squares meet.
Care
Handwash in cool water with mild soap, or machine-wash on a delicates cycle. Lay flat and re-pin the six points while damp to keep the shape.
What to try next

The treble cluster hexagon replaces the open corner ch-2 construction with a solid 5-tr cluster at each point, giving a more defined raised corner. The lacy hexagon opens up the side spaces with double trebles and chain-3 spans for an airy finish.
